title: Rafram bar Pappa (I)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav Chisda’s student, as in [Shabbat 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82a.3), where he interpreted before Rav Chisda.

Rafram bar Pappa transmits teachings in Rav Chisda’s name in [Berakhot 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26a.3) and [59a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.59a.15), [Shabbat 81a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.81a.6), [Eruvin 83a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.83a.4), [Taanit 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.13a.2), [Ketubot 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.4a.3), [Kiddushin 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.81b.14), [Bava Metzia 80b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.80b.13), [Bava Batra 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b.6-7) and [Sanhedrin 48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.48a.9).

In [Niddah 61b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.61b.6-7), Rafram bar Pappa says in Rav Chisda’s name: “A garment in which kilayim was lost — one dyes it and it is permitted.” Rava said to Rafram bar Pappa: “From where does the old man have this?” He said to him: “It is a mishnah.” (Hyman criticizes Dor Dor veDorshav, part 3, end of chapter 16, for thinking that Rava’s question “From where does the old man have this?” referred to Rafram; he considers this an error, since it is explicit that it refers to Rav Chisda, who was then indeed very old.) In [Berakhot 8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.8a.16) Rava said to him: “Let the Master tell us some of the fine things you said in Rav Chisda’s name.” He still merited to know Rav Huna, as in [Taanit 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.20b.11), where Rava said to him: “Let the Master tell us some of the fine things that Rav Huna used to do.” He said to him: “His youth I do not remember; his old age I remember,” and he related to him all his great deeds. Hyman infers from this that he knew Rav Huna even before his advanced old age, and he said only that he did not remember the deeds he did then. He therefore considers it impossible to say that he is the Rafram bar Pappa who headed the academy in Pumbedita and died in year 706 (תשו; era unspecified here), for that was nearly a hundred years after Rav Huna’s death.

He is mentioned in [Yevamot 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.20a.9-10), where he said, “A general rule — to include the rival of an aylonit,” which Hyman describes as contrary to Rav Assi.[^3] And in [Bava Batra 160b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.160b.3-4) he is mentioned before Rami bar Yechezkel. In both places he is mentioned as Rafram without further designation.

notes.text: תשו is706 without era conversion; בדו״ד denotes Dor Dor veDorshav. Hyman’s identification of the old man as Chisda and his chronological separation remain arguments. Supplied Taanitכ. is20a; the saved Davidson20b paragraph10 contains the corresponding Rafram/Huna conversation, noted alongside rather than replacing Hyman’s locator.

The consulted Taanit 20b preserves Rava asking Rafram about Huna and the reply that he remembers the old age, not the youth, followed by Huna’s conduct. It does not independently prove Hyman’s inference that Rafram knew Huna before advanced old age. The supplied 20a, Chisda identification, chronological separation and 706 without an era conversion remain explicit.

[Seder HaDorot 3252](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3252&lang=en) points to [Berakhot 8a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.8a.16), where Rava asks Rafram for teachings in Rav Chisda’s name. Hyman cites Ketubot 8a. In [Yevamot 20a:9–10](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.20a.9-10), the first version has Rafram bar Pappa including the rival in accordance with Rav Assi. The alternate version has Rafram without a patronymic excluding her, contrary to Rav Assi. Heilprin lists the later academy head separately in [Seder HaDorot 3253](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3253&lang=en).
